Fixed. The race was in `src/flight.js`, which had two interlocking bugs:

**Root cause — stale commit (the reported symptom):** when a flight settled, it unconditionally ran `pending.delete(key)` and `commit(value)`. After `invalidate`/`set`/`clear` detached the flight from the registry, its late resolution still wrote the stale value back into the cache — so a reader after invalidation could see the old value. Intermittent in production because it only manifests when the load resolves *after* the invalidation.

**Second bug found while checking failure/mutation paths:** the settle handler also blindly deleted whatever was registered under the key. An obsolete flight settling *after* a fresh flight had started would evict the newer flight from the registry — breaking dedup and letting yet another load start. Additionally, rejections never ran `pending.delete(key)` at all, so a failed load stayed registered forever: every subsequent `get` re-joined the rejected promise instead of retrying, violating "rejected loads are never cached … a subsequent get may retry."

**The fix:** the settle handlers now check `pending.get(key) === promise` — only the flight currently registered for the key may unregister itself and commit. A detached flight still delivers its value/rejection to its original waiters (per contract) but can neither store a value nor clobber a newer flight. Rejections now unregister a current flight so retries work, while the rejection reason still propagates unchanged to all waiters.

Verified against the contract in `src/cache.js` with `node --test` (visible test passes) plus a throwaway suite covering: rejection retry, sync-throw dedup, `set()` winning over a pending load without TTL restart, obsolete flights not detaching newer ones, double-invalidate barriers, `clear()` committing nothing, `ttlMs = 0` dedup-without-reuse, TTL starting at commit time, and `load` synchronously calling `set`/re-reading its own key. `cache.js` and `clock.js` needed no changes; the `createCache` export, API, and dedup semantics are unchanged.
